json.title: F1 2026 Bahrain pre-season test: Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads Mercedes 1-2 on day three
json.content:
Mercedes reaffirmed belief that it is the team to beat in Formula 1 this year after Andrea Kimi Antonelli topped a Silver Arrows 1-2 on the final day of this week’s 2026 Bahrain pre-season test.

The 19-year-old set a 1m33.669s, which was 0.249s quicker than team-mate George Russell, who topped the morning session before Antonelli jumped in the W17 post-lunch.

So, it was the perfect way for Mercedes to overcome a somewhat underwhelming day on Thursday, given a power unit issue ruled out Antonelli for much of the morning running.

Nevertheless, the pair were the only drivers to go sub 1m34s this week amid widespread belief that the German marque heads into 2026’s regulation change as favourite for the championship.

Mercedes boss Toto Wolff has done his best to dispute that tag though, arguing that Red Bull is actually the benchmark, but one team that has gone under the radar in Bahrain is Ferrari.

Yet the Scuderia had a productive Friday as Lewis Hamilton was the quickest non-Mercedes driver, setting a 1m34.209s in the morning leaving him 0.291s off Russell. Hamilton’s day ended 10 minutes early, however, as he went off at Turn 8 with what appeared to be a mechanical issue - a loss of fuel being the prime suspect.

Although F1 managed to squeeze in some green flag running at the very end, it still didn’t threaten Hamilton’s position as Oscar Piastri and Max Verstappen remained fourth and fifth respectively, 0.880s and 1.672s off Antonelli - with both times set during the afternoon.

Verstappen’s new team-mate Isack Hadjar was sixth, while Esteban Ocon (Haas), Franco Colapinto (Alpine), Oliver Bearman (Haas) and Nico Hulkenberg (Audi) completed the top 10.

Lap times aren’t the only thing to analyse in testing, however, as mileage is just as important - if not more. And Piastri completed the most tours of the Bahrain circuit with 161.

That was the most any driver has completed in one day this week and Hamilton (150), Colapinto (144), plus Liam Lawson (119) were the others to hit a century on Friday.

They were obviously helped by running the whole day though, rather than splitting duties with their team-mate. Even so, McLaren still completed the most mileage of any team ahead of Ferrari.

Williams came third on that leaderboard with 146 laps, with Haas fourth (145), Alpine fifth (144) and Mercedes sixth (139), who could have been higher had Antonelli not missed the opening 90 minutes of the afternoon.

Towards the bottom, trouble continued to hit Aston Martin and newcomer Cadillac, which caused the first of two red flags as a cooling issue forced Valtteri Bottas to stop inside the opening hour.

It then took the team nearly two hours to send him back out, leaving it with just 105 laps on Friday while Aston only completed 72 tours. That’s because of an unspecified issue, which kept Lance Stroll out for much of the afternoon running.

This was the first of two official pre-season tests for 2026, with drivers returning to Bahrain for another three-day session on 18-20 February before the Melbourne opener in March.
json.summary: Andrea Kimi Antonelli led a Mercedes 1-2 in the final day of pre-season testing at Bahrain, setting the fastest lap. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton was third fastest. McLaren topped the mileage charts, while new team Cadillac and Aston Martin faced reliability issues.

json.title: Mercedes Has A Future Product Plan That Will Make V8 Fans Very Happy
json.content:
Mercedes Has A Future Product Plan That Will Make V8 Fans Very Happy

Mercedes-Benz is coming off a slow sales year. But the company will be looking to change the tide over the next couple of years. The German brand just issued a strategy update for the new year. The company revealed that it is planning an onslaught of new products from across its sub-brand portfolio. And enthusiasts will be pleased. It looks like V8 engines, which have no end date, will continue to play a prominent role.

Mercedes Will Premiere Seven New Vehicles In The Next Three Months

The Mercedes strategy update spells out plans to launch 30 new vehicles through the end of 2027. Sixteen of those new vehicles will launch in 2026. And Mercedes has confirmed that it will give seven new vehicles a world premiere within the next three months. The strategy update is international. So not all of those forthcoming vehicles may be available in the US market.

Mercedes provided a rough breakdown of the new vehicles it will be launching. Most of them will use internal combustion powertrains. Six of the 16 vehicles coming for 2026 are what Mercedes calls "Top-End" models. Four of those will be combustion vehicles, and two will be EVs. Eight of the 16 new vehicles are "Core" models, with five being combustion vehicles and three being battery-electric. The launches also will include two "Entry-Level" models, one gas-powered and one battery-electric.

Mercedes-Benz 2026 Product Strategy Slide

Models | Combustion | Electric
----------|--------------|-----------
Top-End | 8 | 4
Core | 11 | 4
Entry-Level | 2 | 1

Mercedes is focusing on the "Top-End" market, with 12 new reveals through the end of 2027, compared with just three for the "Entry-Level" market over the next two years. That focus should not be too surprising. Mercedes has been targeting and expanding its upmarket offerings for years due to the profit margins. The "Top-End" models experienced the smallest sales decline among the three categories in 2025. And any instability in the broader economy would likely affect the entry-level side.

Which New Models Will Mercedes-Benz Reveal?

The company did mention some of the Top-End models coming by name. Mercedes already revealed the refreshed S-Class. A refreshed version of the ultra-luxurious Mercedes-Maybach S-Class sedan is on tap for a March reveal. Mercedes is bringing its AMG.EA platform into production, starting with a four-door coupe arriving this year, with an SUV to follow. The "G" sub-brand will also premiere the already-teased Cabriolet version of the G-Class.

Don't Worry About Mercedes-Benz Dropping V8 Engines Anytime Soon

Once upon a time, Mercedes-Benz planned to be all-electric by 2030 and phase out V8 engines in favor of four-cylinder plug-in hybrid powertrains. The brand has backtracked on both fronts, ratcheting back its EV plans, pulling the four-pot AMG C63, and bringing a new V8 engine to market.

Mercedes-Benz confirmed that "high-tech electrified" four-cylinder (gas and diesel), six-cylinder (gas and diesel), and eight-cylinder (gas) combustion engines will remain in production. The company noted that all of those engines meet EU7 regulations. So they will be around for the long haul.

Source: Mercedes-Benz

Inline-six and V8 engines have long been the traditional backbone for the AMG model lineup. Enthusiasts may be glad to note that Mercedes's slide showed an AMG logo next to the six-cylinder and eight-cylinder engines, but not the four-cylinder.
json.summary: Mercedes-Benz plans to launch 30 new models by the end of 2027, including seven world premieres in the next three months. The company confirmed that V8 and six-cylinder engines, particularly for AMG models, will remain in production for the long term, meeting EU7 regulations.

json.title: Opinion: Mercedes-AMG's New Inline-Six Is An Apology For Its Four-Cylinder Mistake
json.content:
Opinion: Mercedes-AMG's New Inline-Six Is An Apology For Its Four-Cylinder Mistake

By Gerhard Horn

Published Feb 12, 2026, 9:02 PM EST

Gerhard started his career in automotive journalism in 2010, after finishing degrees in Communication, English, and Politics, and diplomas in Film and Art Appreciation and Graphic Design. He's currently a senior editor with experience in local and global coverage, and more than 1,000 test cars driven. He started his career at CarBuzz in January 2021.

Try something different:

Show me the facts   Explain it like I’m 5   Give me a lighthearted recap

By the time you read this, the new turbocharged inline-six Mercedes-AMG GLC 53 will have made its debut, showcasing the engine that will replace the unloved turbocharged and electrified powertrain in the snout of the Mercedes-AMG C63. It's way down on power compared to the outgoing top-ranking C-Class, but as customers proved by not buying one, it just doesn't matter. When it comes to performance, noise matters. Why else would automakers spend millions developing sound systems that mimic the sound of a gas-powered car?

Mercedes-Benz AMG C63 Sedan

Sedan

Base Trim Transmission: 9-speed Automatic

Fuel Economy: TBC

Segment: Compact Luxury Performance Sedan

The weirdest thing of all is that it's Mercedes-Benz that fell into this trap. It spends millions on research and development, and yet most of us who love cars just knew that a C63 that dropped half its cylinder count simply wouldn't work. The AMG brand was effectively built on the back of the V8 engine, and that angry V8 rumble has been present on all of its most iconic cars. Think back to the AMG Hammer, the supercharged E55 AMG, SLS, G63, and my personal favorite, the 2008 Mercedes-Benz CLK63 AMG Black Series.

The best thing about an AMG V8 is that you don't have to go all out all the time to enjoy it. Even when idling around, it produces a low-down angry rumble that echoes through the cabin just loud enough to let you know it's there, and willing to partake in whatever buffoonery should you so wish.

Related:  
Driven: The Mercedes-Benz CLK AMG Black Series Is A Modern Classic That Needs Anger Management  
Is it worth well over $100,000 to buy a used one?

Posts

So Why Did AMG Drop So Drastically?

2024 Mercedes-AMG C63 S E Performance on the highway

Mercedes

Mercedes was forced to drop its cylinder count for the same reasons everyone else has. Noise and emissions regulations are getting tougher, which is why the turbocharged inline-six has quickly become the golden standard. And as BMW has been proving since 1968, inline-six engines can be as much fun and equally sonorous as V8s. You don't hear people complain about the power output and sound of the famous S58...

But as we know, Mercedes-AMG dropped from eight to four, skipping six entirely. In my opinion, there are several reasons why. First, the 45 AMG engine did wonders for its hot hatches and crossovers. Secondly, they thought the C63's impressive 670 hp output would grab all the headlines. Finally, Mercedes must have thought that people would be so bowled over by the technological prowess of the car that they wouldn't miss the sound of its famous 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine.

2024 Mercedes-AMG C63 S E Performance

Mercedes

Thankfully, hindsight is 20/20, and it's very clear that AMG customers did not want to pay $90,000 for a four-cylinder C-Class AMG, even if it had 670-hp on tap. I can't help but wonder how many customers Mercedes lost to BMW and Cadillac, both of whom still offer charismatic six-cylinders and manual gearboxes. Heck, even Mercedes-AMG's own E53 was priced so strangely that it was almost a direct rival to the C63.

Why The Six-Cylinder Engine Will Work

Mercedes-AMG CLE 63 Spy Shot

CarBuzz/Valnet

Mercedes recently introduced a new twin-turbocharged V8 with a flat-plane crank. This updated engine made its debut in the facelifted S-Class, still providing loads of torque low-down, once again proving that its engineers are masters of adapting engines for various applications. This engine will likely be used to power the CLE 63 Coupe, leaving the C-Class to cope with a six-cylinder, and that's not a bad thing.

It's historically accurate, for example. The very first C-Class AMG was equipped with an NA inline-six. The W202 C36 AMG is an extremely cool piece of the '90s that you can own for not much money. The C43 and C55 followed, and after that, Mercedes reverted to a supercharged V6 before going back to a series of V8s.

Related:  
This Cheap Straight-Six Mercedes-Benz C-Class AMG Is Slow, But Ridiculously Cool

When looking for a sports sedan, pace is usually the main consideration. With this one, its cool factor is a key USP.

Posts

By Kyle Francis

Secondly, Mercedes-AMG's updated mild-hybrid twin-turbocharged inline-six produces 443 horsepower and 443 pound-feet of torque, with a temporary overboost function unlocking 472 lb-ft for short bursts of speed. Now, that's not even on par with the base detuned BMW M4 with a manual transmission. But the C 53 will be more of a BMW M440i rival, while the previously-mentioned suspected CLE 63 will deal with the M4.

The important thing is that it will perform in all the areas the four-cylinder C63 let the automotive world down. Will the 3.0-liter inline-six sound as good as the V8? No, but that doesn't mean it won't be vocal. I'm going to state that I'm not particularly bowled over with the existing CLE 53's exhaust notes, but it's a million times better than the C63's awkward boy-racer fake sounds, and exuberant pops and bangs.

The second reason I'm looking forward to the car Mercedes-AMG should have built in the first place is the weight loss. The PHEV C63 has a curb weight of 4,817 pounds, which is roughly 1,000 lbs more than the car it replaced. The 53 engine is only a mild hybrid, which means Mercedes-AMG can rip all the plug-in garbage and the heavy battery out of it. We can only estimate at this point, but the CLE 53 with the same setup weighs 4,420 lbs. The sedan will likely be a bit heavier, but it's clear that a massive weight saving is in the cards.

Is It What We Wanted?

2027 Mercedes-AMG GLC 53 Coupe

Mercedes-AMG

It's a step in the right direction, at least. Mercedes-AMG made a huge mistake, and this is a nice apology. Recent developments in the automotive world have made the 4.0 V8 relevant again, and it will be nice to see it back in a small car, but, for now, this is perfectly adequate.

2015 Mercedes-AMG C63 Sedan AMG C 63 S Sedan

Engine: 4.0L Twin-Turbo V8 Gas

Drivetrain: Rear-Wheel Drive

Transmission: 7-Speed Automatic

Horsepower: 503 hp

Torque: 516 lb-ft @ 1750 rpm

Find 2015 Mercedes-AMG C63 Sedan and more cars for sale on our Marketplace

Shop Now

Having said that, an adequate amount of power is not the AMG way. If previous versions of the C63 taught us anything, it's that you start off with too much power, and then you add some more for good measure. Luckily, there is an easy fix. A used W205 Mercedes-AMG C63 is currently the most affordable way to get AMG's sweet 4.0 V8 in your life. If the new six-cylinder isn't your thing, it's nice to know you can still shop around on the used market to satisfy the demand for that V8 grumble.

Related:  
The Cheapest Used Car Equipped With Mercedes-AMG's Famous 4.0 Twin-Turbocharged V8

The last of a dying breed

Sources: Mercedes-AMG.
json.summary: Mercedes-AMG is replacing the high-horsepower but unpopular four-cylinder hybrid powertrain in its C63 with a new turbocharged inline-six. The new engine, to debut in models like the GLC 53, offers less power but promises better sound, reduced weight, and a more traditional AMG driving experience.

json.title: Sinking star: Mercedes operating profits dropped by more than 50%
json.content:
Following a year marked by US tariffs and severe competition from China, the German car manufacturer Mercedes recorded a huge drop in operating profits in 2025.

Analysts expected Mercedes-Benz to report poor figures but the €5.8bn in operating profits for 2025, announced this Thursday, were significantly lower than the predicted €6.6bn.

The car manufacturer's operating profits fell by 57% and turnover fell by 9% last year.

This is mainly due to the poor sales figures in China, which fell by 19% compared to 2024. China remains the most important market for the German car making behemoth, with almost a third of all Mercedes cars sold there.

In addition to the "intense competition with China," Mercedes-Benz cites "global tariffs and negative exchange rate effects" as reasons for the slump in profits.

Moreover, the company has not been able to smoothly transition to the EV market.

"In a dynamic market environment, our financial results were in line with our forecast, driven by a clear focus on efficiency, speed and flexibility," Mercedes boss Ola Källenius said in response to the group's poor figures.

Mercedes-Benz is expecting to increase profits in 2026, particularly through planned cost cuts as well as several new product launches. The company is targeting an adjusted return on sales of 5% from the current 3%.

However, as it stands, profits at Mercedes-Benz have fallen for the third year in a row. The firm's shares are trading around 7% lower than at the start of the year due to the negative trajectory.

The DAX-listed company has already initiated a comprehensive savings programme. The company explains that "cost savings of more than €3.5 billion at Mercedes-Benz Cars" compensated for some of the headwinds.

In the medium term, Mercedes-Benz expects to sell around 2 million vehicles and intends to double the amount of EV sales.

The company is trying to motivate employees and potential buyers with words of praise, claiming the "team has done an outstanding job in 2025. We have successfully launched our biggest product and technology offensive to date and introduced cutting-edge technologies."

However, the German car manufacturer faces challenges such as supply chain disruptions, rising production costs, and other regulatory pressures.
json.summary: Mercedes-Benz reported a 57% drop in operating profits to €5.8 billion for 2025, worse than expected. The slump was driven by a 19% sales decline in China, intense competition, global tariffs, and a challenging transition to electric vehicles. The company has launched a cost-cutting program.

json.title: Mercedes and Red Bull hit trouble on second Bahrain F1 test day
json.content:
Mercedes and Red Bull hit trouble on second Bahrain F1 test day

Mercedes was struck by a power unit issue at Bahrain Formula 1 testing, while Red Bull suffered a two-hour delay on Thursday morning

Filip Cleeren

Edited: Feb 12, 2026, 3:23 PM

The Mercedes Formula 1 team has encountered its second issue of the Bahrain test, with Andrea Kimi Antonelli's W17 breaking down after just three laps with a power unit issue.

Mercedes had been reliably racking up miles at Barcelona's shakedown, but its running in Bahrain has now been halted for two consecutive days. On Wednesday afternoon Antonelli was restricted to 30 laps with a suspension problem, after George Russell had completed 56 laps in the morning session.

Antonelli has now been dealt another setback after his Mercedes' new power unit suffered an issue after just three laps, requiring Mercedes to replace the entire power unit as it aims to make it back out in the afternoon.

Russell is scheduled to take over again after the lunch break, but given the mileage completed is now being skewed towards him, Mercedes may well adjust its run programme on Thursday or Friday to hand Antonelli more time aboard the W17.

Meanwhile, Red Bull has also been kept in the garage after what the team said was a "routine issue during the car build" relating to a hydraulic leak, which has caused a two-hour delay.

That is eating into Isack Hadjar's track time, with the Frenchman scheduled to take the reins of the RB22 for the entire day.

Mercedes powered teams had been talking up Red Bull-Ford's alleged advantage with its new hybrid power units, which comes against the backdrop of rival manufacturers trying to nix Mercedes' interpretation of the regulations around engine compression ratios.

At the start of Thursday's running, Sergio Perez caused the first red flag of the day after his Cadillac coasted a halt on the Mexican's outlap. After the car was recovered, Perez was able to return to the track an hour later.
json.summary: Mercedes halted early with a power unit failure, forcing a full engine replacement. Red Bull lost two hours to a hydraulic leak. The issues disrupted scheduled track time for drivers Antonelli and Hadjar.

json.title: Mercedes duo leads the way on final day in Sakhir
json.content:
Mercedes duo leads the way on final day in Sakhir

by Speedway Digest Staff

February 13, 2026

Reading Time: 3 mins read

The first pre-season test in Bahrain concluded with a Mercedes one-two at the top of the timesheets. Kimi Antonelli set the fastest lap of 1:33.669s, beating teammate George Russell by 0.249s. Behind them, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton clocked a 1:34.209s. All three drivers, running on the C3 compound, were not only the quickest today but recorded the fastest times overall across the three days in Sakhir.

Taking the full 24 hours of track activity from Wednesday to Friday into account, Antonelli and Russell are the only drivers to have broken the 1:34 barrier. Oscar Piastri (McLaren), who finished the day fourth, set the best times on the two hardest compounds, posting a 1:36.234s on the C2 and a 1:36.899s on the C1. However, these benchmarks still stand to the credit of Lando Norris (McLaren) for the C2 (1:34.669s) and Max Verstappen (Red Bull) for the C1 (1:35.631s).

Following yesterday’s trend, several teams focused on race simulations. Piastri pushed a set of C1s for 24 laps and a set of C2s for 22 laps. The longest runs on the C3 were completed by the two Mercedes drivers, with 18 laps each.

Mario Isola, Pirelli Motorsport Director: “These first three days of testing in Bahrain have been useful in confirming, following the shakedown week in Barcelona, that the results gathered during last year’s development tests with mule cars are sufficiently representative. Compound characteristics seem to be in line with expectations and feedback from drivers has been positive. The new compounds have maintained good mechanical resistance, reducing the appearance of graining, as verified over the last few days, and seem to keep overheating under control.

It is clear that drivers are still adapting to the power delivery system. Evidence of some flat spots on the tyres suggests that drivers may have changed their approach to corners. On corner exit, by contrast, the electric power delivery tends to make the rear axle slip, increasing the surface temperature of the tyres and causing a slight loss of grip.

Next week, we expect teams to focus more on performance runs, though likely without revealing their full potential. Combined with the race simulations from these past few days, we will have a clearer picture of what to expect for the start of the season. This will allow us to refine the compound selections for races from Miami onwards, the first event for which tyres have not yet been shipped.”

Throughout today’s 8-hour session, teams most frequently opted for the C3 compound, which covered 687 laps (48%). The C2 reached 431 laps (30%), while the hardest C1 covered 306 laps (21%). As expected, there were no surprises in these figures. Temperatures were slightly higher than on Wednesday and Thursday; the track reached 44°C (with a minimum of 27°C), while ambient air stayed between 27°C and 33°C.

Lando Norris, Pierre Gasly (Alpine), Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin), Charles Leclerc (Ferrari), and Arvin Lindblad (Racing Bulls) did not drive today.

Across the three days of testing at the Bahrain International Circuit, a total of 20.673 kilometres were covered by all cars, with 51% of that distance on the C3. Regarding sets used, the softest option (C3) saw 144 sets, compared to 79 for the C2 and 42 for the C1.

Teams and drivers now have a brief rest before the next session begins next Wednesday, again in Bahrain. While only the three hardest slick compounds were available this week, the next test will allow teams to choose an allocation of 24 sets including the full Pirelli range from C1 to C5. It will also be possible to carry over used sets of the first test week with no more than 9 laps on them.

Pirelli PR
json.summary: Mercedes drivers Kimi Antonelli and George Russell set the fastest times on the final day of F1 pre-season testing in Sakhir, Bahrain. Antonelli posted the quickest lap, with teammate Russell close behind, as teams completed race simulations and gathered data for the upcoming season.

json.title: BYD and Geely compete to buy Nissan–Mercedes Benz plant in Aguascalientes
json.content:
Two of China's leading automakers, BYD and Geely, are among the finalists to buy a Nissan–Mercedes-Benz plant in Mexico, according to a person familiar with the matter, as China seeks to manufacture in a country where U.S. tariffs are causing factory closures and layoffs.

The two finalists emerged from among nine companies that expressed interest in acquiring the plant, including at least two other major Chinese manufacturers: Chery and Great Wall Motor, according to two sources familiar with the matter. Vietnamese electric vehicle manufacturer VinFast is the third finalist, one of the people said.

The interest from Chinese manufacturers, which had not been previously reported, represents a potentially significant shift in Mexico's automotive industry. For decades, U.S., European, and Japanese manufacturers have dominated the market, building primarily vehicles destined for the United States.

Now, Mexican officials face a balancing act. Tariffs imposed by the Trump administration are hurting Mexico's automotive sector, and Chinese investment could generate much-needed jobs, but they also fear that Chinese production in the Latin American country could irritate Washington and jeopardize this year's negotiations on the North American trade agreement, known as T-MEC.

The United States has effectively banned the sale of Chinese-brand vehicles, and President Donald Trump has accused Mexico of providing a back door for Chinese products to enter the U.S. market.

BYD, Chery, Great, Geely, VinFast, and Wall did not immediately respond to Reuters' inquiries on the matter.

BYD and Geely's manufacturing ambitions in Mexico underscore the explosive global growth of China's auto industry. BYD's vehicle sales have increased tenfold since 2020, and Geely's have doubled. Both companies sold more than 4 million vehicles last year, roughly the same as Ford.
json.summary: Chinese automakers BYD and Geely are finalists to purchase a Nissan-Mercedes plant in Aguascalientes, Mexico. The move highlights China's push for North American manufacturing as U.S. tariffs pressure Mexico's auto sector, but risks complicating U.S.-Mexico trade relations.

json.title: Williams: Rival F1 teams 'pissed off' over Mercedes engine, but it's fully legal
json.content:
Williams: Rival F1 teams 'pissed off' over Mercedes engine, but it's fully legal

James Vowles, Williams Racing Team Principal, says Mercedes has pushed the absolute limit with its new engine, but it is fully legal. He adds that F1 should not risk becoming "a BOP series" 

Ronald Vording

Published: Feb 11, 2026, 8:31 AM

At the start of winter testing in Bahrain, most discussions in the Formula 1 paddock revolve around two words: compression ratio. Rivals are keeping a close eye on the Mercedes power unit, which complies with the 16:1 limit during static tests, but can achieve a higher ratio while running on track.

Audi, Ferrari and Honda immediately asked for clarification in a joint letter to the FIA, with Red Bull’s position understood to be more nuanced than initially thought. It is now up to the FIA to answer the question of whether it wants to adjust the measurement procedures or not — and if so, on what timeframe.

Read Also: 
 Formula 1Mercedes rivals push for intervention over F1 engine loophole - but how realistic is it? 

A first step in that process would be the required supermajority in the Power Unit Advisory Committee, with four of the five engine manufacturers as well as the FIA and FOM.

However, Vowles makes it clear that he would see such an intervention as completely against the DNA of F1.

“My harsh line on it is the PU that we have in the car is completely compliant with the regulations. It is not a month of work but several years of work to produce the PU to that level. We, as a sport, have to take care that this is not a BOP series. This is a meritocracy where the best engineering outcome effectively gets rewarded as a result, not punished as a result,” Vowles told media, including Motorsport.com.

“I'm sure other teams are pissed off. They weren't able to achieve what Mercedes did, but we also need to take care. Right now, I don't think there's a person in the pitlane that can tell you what is the best PU, and we only focus on one detail of it.

“My hope is that sense prevails and that we, as a sport, recognise that we are here to be a meritocracy, and that the best engineering solution wins as a result of it. Therefore we are where we are right now, but I maintain that our PU is completely compliant with all regulations.”

Vowles emphasised that it is precisely for this reason — that Mercedes pushes the absolute limit — that he was determined to have a Mercedes power unit in the Williams cars.

“I've been with Mercedes for 23 years, pretty much from the start of my career that's what I've always been a part of. The day I joined \[this team\], I re-signed the Mercedes arrangement here at Williams for pretty much that reason – which is that they are incredibly good at regulation changes, reading the rules exactly as the rules are, and making sure you push the boundaries of engineering. That is exactly what the PU represents right now for Mercedes.”

Changing the procedures is more complex than it seems

Vowles added that adjusting the measurement methods is easier said than done.

“First of all, they have to come up with a regulation, and good luck with them, where you're testing power units in the conditions you're trying to run on track. Anyone that knows anything about compression ratios, even if you've done your own cars, you kind of want to do it when it's ambient.

“I'm sure they can determine a way of testing it, but the next element is that there are now two more steps. One: are we compliant even with any future regulation changes? No one knows that one particularly. And the second element of things is what do you do when you have effectively changed the rules? That now means that if we are not legal to it, that there are eight cars not participating on the grid. And that's what I meant by we, as a sport, have to really think about what the implication of this change is.”

George Russell, Mercedes

In defence of the FIA, the Williams team principal acknowledged that the governing body can never keep everyone in the paddock satisfied and that regulating F1 is an extremely difficult task, especially at the start of a new regulatory cycle.

“To defend the FIA, the FIA has a hard job. You have teams filled with a thousand individuals thinking about how we can interpret the rules in a clever way. Let’s be blunt about it, that's what teams do, and that's why we love the sport. It is difficult \[for the FIA\]. There's 20-odd people trying to fight against 10,000 out there on the grid. It's probably not that amount, but you get the idea behind it.

“The FIA do a really good job, generally speaking, of finding the boundary between clever interpretation and allowing it to go forward. What I'm stating here is that we need to take care that it's not just politically driven by other teams that didn't think of clever innovations now, and the FIA's job is to take a correct line of action on all of this.”

json.title: The Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG V12 Will Give You A Massive Smile, And Even Bigger Engine Bills
json.content:
If you’re looking for a seriously fast sedan that effortlessly evades attention, this one deserves a long, hard look. With an exterior that screams “retired executive,” the AMG S65 sedan, based on the W220-generation Mercedes-Benz S-Class, is the kind of car that disappears into traffic. However, it's a genuine rocket when you need it to be. It was even pegged as the world’s fastest sedan upon its 2004 debut, a claim that wasn’t exactly marketing fluff.

At the time, only a handful of elite supercars could outrun it, and even by today's standards, the W220 S65’s straight-line pace is seriously quick.

Mercedes-Benz AMG S65 Sedan

Sedan

Base: $235,600

Find 2020 Mercedes-AMG S65 Sedan and more cars for sale on our Marketplace

It’s also cheap in today's market, though finding one for sale is the real challenge. The W220-generation S65 AMG was offered in the US for 2006 only, and total imports totaled well fewer than a thousand. Your best bet is the online collector-car auctions, where high-mileage examples (think north of 100,000 miles) can dip to around $15,000, while cleaner cars command $30,000 or more. Prices have been creeping upward in recent years, signaling early collector status, but current prices are still pocket change compared to the roughly $170,000 sticker the car carried when new.

A Flagship For Both Mercedes And AMG

2006 Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG Front 3/4 View

Mercedes-Benz

| 2006 Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG |                                 |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| Engine                     | Twin-turbocharged 6.0-liter V12 |
| Transmission               | 5-speed automatic               |
| Drivetrain                 | Rear-wheel drive                |
| Power                      | 604 hp                          |
| Torque                     | 738 lb-ft                       |
| 0-60 mph                   | 4.4 seconds                     |
| Top Speed                  | 155 mph (limited)               |

The W220-generation S-Class, introduced for the 2000 model year in the US, isn’t exactly beloved among S-Class fans – quite the opposite, in fact. It was developed to be significantly lighter than the vault-like W140 it replaced but the result made it feel cheaper – an impression only worsened by reliability issues that would emerge later, including early rust, electronic gremlins, and problematic suspension. It did, however, offer plenty of performance thanks to AMG.

For 2001, AMG launched the S55 with a 360-horsepower 5.4-liter V8. While brisk, this model lacked the freight-train shove enthusiasts expected, so a supercharger arrived for 2003, boosting output to 493 hp. A twin-turbocharged V12 followed, giving us the first S65. For reasons that remain unclear, the S65 reached the US more than a year after its initial launch, arriving for the 2006 model year – the W220’s final year. As a result, few were sold stateside, and those that were suffered steep depreciation once the next-generation W221 S65 arrived just a year later.

2006 Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG Badge

Mercedes-Benz

As a flagship for both Mercedes and AMG, the S65 was loaded with tech. This included an automatic transmission with a manual mode and steering wheel-mounted shifters, reinforced to handle the high torque load. The engine – known as the M275 – delivered peak torque between 2,000 and 4,000 rpm, though it had to be electronically limited to prevent drivetrain damage. The real figure is thought to have been closer to 885 lb-ft.

Beyond the powertrain, another standout was Active Body Control, Mercedes’ then-new active suspension. Using hydraulics and sensors to counteract body movement, the system on the S65 was tuned for dynamic performance, including firmer damping. Electronic chassis systems, including ABS, stability control, and traction control, were also relaxed to allow more spirited driving. Stopping power came from one of AMG’s largest brake setups yet, with eight-piston calipers up front.

Fast, Even Two Decades On

2006 Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG Side View

Mercedes-Benz

Behind the wheel of the 2006 S65 AMG, drivers will quickly notice how dominant its performance remains today. Flooring the throttle produces a brief lag before a surge of power arrives, delivering relentless shove through every gear. The official 0-60 time of 4.4 seconds is probably conservative – something that's all the more impressive when you consider there are over 5,000 lbs to hustle.

A lot of that weight is due to the big V12, which weighs more than 550 lbs, and you feel that heavy nose in tighter corners. The S65 isn’t a sports car through curves, but it’s remarkably composed for a luxury barge. Thanks to AMG‑specific suspension tuning, the car mitigates much of the bulk’s pitch and roll, making high‑speed sweepers confidence‑inspiring rather than unsettling, though sharper turns still require some care. Thankfully, the brakes provide ample stopping power, letting you scrub speed effectively before entering any bend.

2003 - 2006 Mercedes-AMG S55 interior

Mercedes

Inside, the S65’s cabin blends opulence with purposeful refinement. Plush Nappa leather and real wood trim envelop you in classic Mercedes luxury, and while the design may feel slightly dated, the quality is undeniable. Seats are supremely comfortable on long runs, and isolation from wind and road noise reinforces the sense of cocooned refinement. Model-specific touches include AMG gauge clusters, an AMG sports steering wheel, and chrome-finished door sill plates featuring the AMG logo.

Related 

The Biggest Engine Ever In A Series Production Mercedes S-Class

The Mercedes-Benz S-Class is one of the most respected luxury cars on the road, but the version with the largest engine came long ago.

Posts

By Kyle Francis 

What To Watch Out For

2006 Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG Rear View

Mercedes-Benz

After the success of the Lexus LS in the early 1990s, Mercedes knew it had to make the S-Class more competitive. With the introduction of the W220 generation in 1998, we got a lighter, more approachable S-Class compared with the tank-like W140 it replaced, one loaded with new electronic features and cutting-edge technology.

Unfortunately, all that sophistication came at a cost. Reliability has suffered in some areas, and repairs on the more complex systems – particularly the Active Body Control suspension and V12 components – can be jaw-droppingly expensive, sometimes exceeding what the car itself is worth.

Because of the car’s age and rarity, hard data on reliability is limited. ResearchTheCar cites coil pack failures, valve cover gasket leaks, issues with the turbochargers, and the ABC hydraulic suspension as common pain points. Vincheck also highlights electronic gremlins, including problems with infotainment systems, sensors, and control modules.

2003 - 2006 Mercedes-AMG S55 interior

Mercedes

Together, these factors paint a picture of a car that demands careful attention and proactive maintenance to remain functional. As a result, buying a 2006 S65 almost certainly means high maintenance and repair costs, and sourcing specialized parts could be a challenge due to the car's rarity. A thorough mechanical inspection is essential before committing, as even minor oversights can become expensive headaches.

Related 

Mercedes Unlocks The Secret To New Straight-Six, V8, And V12 Engines

You've never seen tech like this in an engine before.

Posts 14

By Evan Williams

Don’t Overlook The S55

2003 - 2006 Mercedes-AMG S55 exterior

Mercedes

Before the W220-generation S-Class spawned the S65, there was already a tamer S55 – but make no mistake, this was a proper AMG. Offered from 2001 to 2006, it began life with a naturally aspirated 5.4-liter V8 making 360 hp, and from 2003 onward a supercharged version pushed output to 493 hp. While not quite as extreme as the S65, the S55 still delivers exhilarating performance. And thanks to higher production numbers, these cars trade on the used market for a fraction of their V12 siblings, with well-kept examples under 100,000 miles available for around $10,000, making them an attractive option for bargain hunters.

Performance-wise, the S55 was only slightly slower than the S65, and with its simpler V8 engine – and the fact that most arrived without the complex Active Body Control suspension – reliability and maintenance should be noticeably easier. Its engine was also used across multiple Mercedes models, so parts are generally more available. Lower running costs and strong performance make the S55 a compelling alternative; it’s a car that deserves a serious look.

Related 

The Most Affordable Used AMG Models You Can Buy In 2025

Some models have become surprisingly affordable.

Posts 6

By Anthony Capretto

The Sleeper King

2006 Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG (W220) Front View

Mercedes-Benz

The 2006 S65 AMG remains one of the great stealth missiles: absurd speed, innocuous looks, and a price tag that still feels like a steal. It delivers supercar punch wrapped in leather and wood, but ownership is not for the faint of heart. Any car from the W220 generation can be a minefield of poor reliability: keep this in mind before you decide to add one to your garage. Choose wisely, inspect obsessively, and budget generously.

Sources: Mercedes-Benz, ResearchTheCar, Vincheck
json.summary: The 2006 Mercedes-Benz S65 AMG, featuring a 604-hp twin-turbo V12, delivers supercar-level speed in an unassuming luxury sedan. Though now affordable on the used market, often priced between $15,000 and $30,000, it is notorious for extremely high maintenance and repair costs.

json.title: Antonelli’s Mercedes Speeds On Day Three In Bahrain
json.content:
Antonelli’s Mercedes Speeds On Day Three In Bahrain

By SPEED SPORT Staff

February 13, 2026

SAKHIR, Bahrain. — The first Formula 1 pre-season test in Bahrain concluded with a Mercedes one-two at the top of the timesheets.

Kimi Antonelli set the fastest lap of 1:33.669, beating teammate George Russell by 0.249 seconds. Behind them, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton clocked a 1:34.209. All three drivers, running on the C3 compound, were not only the quickest today but recorded the fastest times overall across the three days.

Taking the full 24 hours of track activity from Wednesday to Friday into account, Antonelli and Russell are the only drivers to have broken the 1:34 barrier.

Oscar Piastri was fourth for McLaren, while the Red Bulls of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar were fifth and sixth.

Esteban Ocon and Oliver Bearman were seventh and ninth, respectively, for Haas F1.

Nico Hulkenburg put Audi 10th on the board with Sergio Perez 14th for Cadillac.

Lando Norris, Pierre Gasly (Alpine), Fernando Alonso (Aston Martin), Charles Leclerc (Ferrari), and Arvin Lindblad (Racing Bulls) did not drive today.

Across the three days of testing at the Bahrain International Circuit, a total of 20,673 kilometers were covered by all cars.

Teams and drivers now have a brief rest before the next session begins next Wednesday, again in Bahrain.
json.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli set the fastest lap on the final day of Formula 1 pre-season testing in Bahrain, leading a team one-two over teammate George Russell. Their times were the fastest overall across the three-day test.

json.title: Mercedes Teases A Flood Of New Models Coming Soon
json.content:
Mercedes is planning to introduce dozens of new models. S-Class Maybach arrives in March, AMG GT also due this year. 16 new models coming in 2026, while 14 are slated for 2027.

Mercedes held their capital markets day presentation yesterday and announced plans to stage seven world premieres in the next three months. That’s an impressive number, especially considering the company has already introduced the facelifted S-Class and GLC 53.

The automaker didn’t delve into many specifics, but confirmed the new Mercedes-Maybach S-Class debuts in March. The company added the AMG GT 4-Door arrives later this year, while the SUV variant follows in 2027. That year will also see the unveiling of the G-Class Cabriolet.

More: New Mercedes G-Class Cabrio Teased As Testing Begins

While details are light, a slide suggested Mercedes will introduce 16 vehicles this year. Six of them will be fully electric, while the others will have internal combustion engines.

Many of these will be “Top-End” vehicles, which implies we can expect a number of new S-Class variants including the aforementioned Maybach. Some of the others are presumably AMG versions.

As for the Top-End EVs, spy photographers have snapped a facelifted EQS on multiple occasions. It’s expected to feature starry lighting units, a new 800 volt electrical architecture, and an upgraded powertrain. The latter could combine an improved battery with more efficient motors.

2026 will also see the introduction of five Core ICE-powered vehicles and three EVs. One of the latter appears to be the new GLC EQ L for China, which was mentioned in one of the presentations.

On the Entry side of things, there will be a new ICE and EV model. It will join the CLA and GLB, suggesting this could be the redesigned GLA.

2027 will see the introduction of 14 models, three of which will be fully electric. A vast majority of these will become part of the brand’s Core family, while some of the Top-End models could be the facelifted SL.

Mercedes also mentioned a new long-wheelbase GLE for China, which will presumably be based on the facelifted crossover. However, it’s unclear when either model will arrive.

Financials

Fun stuff aside, Mercedes announced adjusted earnings before interest and taxes fell from €13.7 ($16.3) billion in 2024 to €8.2 ($9.7) billion last year. The company blamed the drop on challenges in China, tariffs, and foreign exchange headwinds. On the bright side, the company reduced research and development costs related to future architectures and technologies.

Investors probably won’t like the news, nor will they be thrilled by the proposed dividend of €3.50 ($4.15) per share. That’s significantly less than last year’s payout of €4.30 ($5.10).
json.summary: Mercedes-Benz detailed its 2026-2027 model rollout, including 16 new vehicles this year and 14 next. Confirmed arrivals include the Mercedes-Maybach S-Class in March, the AMG GT 4-Door later in 2026, and the G-Class Cabriolet and AMG SUV variant in 2027.

json.title: Super Pole Beckons After STM Mercedes Tops Qualifying
json.content:
Super Pole Beckons After STM AMG Tops Qualifying

Electric pace requires a 2:01 to get into the top 10; GMR, Ferrari, and reigning champs miss the cut

14 February 2026, 5:05 AM

Cameron Waters has topped an electric Qualifying session at the Bathurst 12 Hour with an incredible 2:01.5631 in the #222 Scott Taylor Motorsport Mercedes. Waters continued his great pace from Practice 6 to set the fastest lap of Qualifying 2 with only seconds left in the session.

His time was the climax of a frantic final 13 minutes, after the session was restarted after a Red Flag to recover the stricken #100 Grove Racing Mercedes, which lost a wheel coming out of the pits.

Once the #100 Mercedes-AMG was recovered, it was all guns blazing as everyone finally showed their hand to try to get into the top 10. It was Christopher Haase in the #55 Jamec Racing Audi who fired first, hitting the top with a 2:01.88 to get the ball rolling. Marco Mapelli hit a 2:01 in the #93 Wall Racing Lamborghini next, before Scott Andrews joined him in the #44 Geyer Valmont Mercedes.

Andrews then stretched the margin, going top with a 2:01.67 to set the fastest lap of the weekend with only three minutes left, before Waters got on track and bested the lot, setting a 2:01.5631 to take the provisional pole by a tenth of a second.

Broc Feeney slotted the #64 HRT Mustang into third behind Andrews, with Luca Stolz and Jayden Ojeda rounding out the top five in the 75 Express Mercedes and #6 Tigani Motorsport AMG, respectively, making it four Mercedes AMGs in the top five.

“I’m stoked,” Feeney said. "To improve from where we were to third in qualifying is a testament to HRT Ford Racing and the Mustang GT3. We worked really hard for that result, and the Mustang is genuinely fast.

“Third position in the first part of qualifying, and advancing to fight for pole position, is truly exciting.”

Completing the top 10 was Haase, who didn’t improve from his 2:01.88, then Raffaele Marciello in the #46 Team WRT BMW. Lucas Auer was eighth in the #77 Craft Bamboo AMG – the only car to stay in the 10 from Q1 – followed by Matt Campbell in the #911 Absolute Racing Porsche, then Marco Mapelli’s #93 Wall Racing Lamborghini.

Craft Bamboo were cool and calm in Q1, with Auer sitting in the pit lane right up until 10 minutes left in the session before heading out for their first venture on track. It proved to be the right move; Lucas Auer put the #77 Mercedes into the 2’s with his first flyer, setting a 2:02.1, and then improved to a 2:01.9715 to top the session.

“We took the risk, we wanted to do the lap time at the end with maximum track evolution,” Auer said after the session. “We knew if there was a red flag, well, that’s how it is.

“But now we did a good time, and it will be interesting to see if we’re in [The Pirelli Pole Battle] because the second group is usually quicker.”

Incredibly, the cut-off time to get into the top 10 was Mapelli’s 2:01.9902, with the top 10 separated by only 0.42 of a second. 8 of the top 10 were Pro-Class cars, with Andrews putting the Pro-Am #44 Geyer Valmont Mercedes into the mix, and Mapelli’s #93 Wall Racing Lamborghini the lead Bronze challenger.

While the top 10 progress to this afternoon’s Pirelli Pole Battle, the remaining positions are set on the grid for the race tomorrow.

Just outside were a pair of BMWs, including the reigning champions – Kelvin van der Linde’s lap in the #32 WRT BMW, only good enough for 12th. Also missing the cut was Laurin Heinrich in the #61 EBM Porsche, who was second in Q1 with a 2:02.3 – only good enough for 13th place.

Neither Ferrari nor Corvette made the top 10, with Ryan Wood putting the #193 Ziggo Sport Tempesta Ferrari into 17th, while Earl Bamber could only manage 25th in the #2 Johor Motorsport Racing Corvette.

One of the stories to come out of Q1 was the #888 Mercedes AMG Team GMR, who ended the session with a 2:06.3, qualifying behind the lead Invitational car. Maro Engel stepped out of the car with over 10 minutes left in Q1, explaining that the Mercedes had suffered an issue.

“We would have loved to have had a crack,” Engel told the broadcasters. “We had a power-related issue, so we’ll have to investigate now and make sure we’re ready for tomorrow.”

It will have to be a great run for the #888 Team GMR if they are to feature tomorrow.

The top Invitational-class car was Glen Wood in the #50 Vantage KTM X-Bow GT2, with a 2:05.76, while the sole remaining GT4 runner, the #42 Method Motorsport McLaren, set a 2:20.6.

The Pirelli Pole Battle hits the track at 15:15 local time (AEDT, UTC+11) for a 15-minute hit-out for the top 10 spots on the grid.
json.summary: Cameron Waters in the #222 Scott Taylor Motorsport Mercedes set the fastest lap of 2:01.5631 in a dramatic Bathurst 12 Hour qualifying session. The top ten cars, separated by just 0.42 seconds, advance to a Super Pole shootout, while notable entries including reigning champions missed the cut.

json.title: George Russell: Red Bull's F1 advantage is 'scary,' don't look at Mercedes
json.content:
George Russell is adamant that Red Bull holds an early advantage in Formula 1 2026, claiming its engine advantage is "scary" and that nobody "should be looking" at Mercedes as the team to beat.

Continuing the back-and-forth between the two teams at the start of the season, however, Red Bull technical director Pierre Waché believes the team are "not the benchmark" and lie fourth behind Mercedes, McLaren and Ferrari.

Both Toto Wolff and Max Verstappen have had contrasting views about Mercedes and Red Bull's pace at preseason testing in Bahrain, where neither team have yet showed their full hand, but both look competitive on track despite McLaren and Ferrari topping the opening two days.

Red Bull's engine -- produced by Red Bull for the first time in 2026 after the split with Honda -- has been drawing praise in particular, with Russell claiming it has the most competitive package.

"I don't think anybody should really be looking at us, you should be looking at the most competitive car on the grid which right now is the Red Bull," Russell said.

"They're not just a small step ahead, you're talking in the order of half a second to a second in deployment over the course of a lap, so it's pretty scary to see that difference.

George Russell believes Max Verstappen's Red Bull has the fastest car.

"Red Bull have always delivered a very good car over the past 15 years even when they didn't have a great engine, so this test has been really eye opening for a lot of us."

Verstappen set the pace early on Wednesday in Bahrain, and Russell added: "The truth is Red Bull in Barcelona Day 1 hit the ground running and were well ahead of all of their competitors, so ourselves, Ferrari and the others.

"Day 1 here in Bahrain again, they sort of knocked it out of the park, so they are, at the moment they're very much a team to beat and it's quite straightforward when you have three days of testing in the same location to make those improvements.

"But when you get to Melbourne and you've got three hours of practice before qualifying, based on what we've seen in Barcelona and Bahrain, Red Bull are going to be ahead. So yeah, we've got work to do."

Toto Wolff: Red Bull, not Mercedes, the F1 2026 benchmark

Speaking shortly before Russell, it's fair to say Waché -- on media duties for Red Bull with team boss Laurent Mekies absent -- didn't quite agree with the Briton's sentiments.

"We are not the benchmark, for sure," he said.

"We see clearly the top three teams, Ferrari, Mercedes and McLaren are in front of us, outside, from our analysis, and we are behind. But there is a work where we think we are. I find it difficult to say about those because the run plan of everybody, the level of fuel they run, the level of power they run is difficult to say, but it's currently our analysis that it could be wrong.

"We don't spend too much time on that. We try to focus on how to improve our work."
json.summary: Mercedes driver George Russell has identified Red Bull as the clear early front-runner for 2026, stating their engine advantage is a 'scary' half to one second per lap. In contrast, Red Bull's technical director downplays their pace, claiming they are fourth fastest.

json.title: Scott Taylor AMG Fastest Ahead Of Qualifying
json.content:
Scott Taylor AMG Fastest Ahead Of Qualifying

Final practice sees top 50% progress to Q2

14 February 2026, 1:48 AM

Cam Waters put the #222 Scott Taylor Motorsport Mercedes on top of the final practice session of the weekend, with a 2:02.35 on his penultimate lap.

“We’re just seeing what we’ve got in the car,” Waters said to the host broadcaster post-session. “I feel like there are a fair few not showing their hand at the moment.

“We obviously want to start at the front of the race, in the clean air with the fast cars. Obviously, pole would be nice, but as long as we’re up the front, and we can get a good start, we’ll be right.”

The morning’s session started in overcast conditions and would determine the placings for Qualifying 1 and 2 later today. The goal? Make it to the top 17 to ensure a spot in Q2 for a clear shot at a good qualifying lap.

It took a while for the pace to really wind up, with the teams still completing race validation runs through the first half of the session. The best time approaching the halfway point was “only” a 2:03.6 from the #911 Absolute Racing Porsche by Matt Campbell.

This included runs from Roman De Angeles in the #27 Heart of Racing by SPS Mercedes and Maxime Martin in the #888 GMR Team Mercedes, who both set purple times (session best) to the second sector, but aborted those laps and came into the pits, hiding their outright pace.

It was at the halfway point that the first shots were fired in anger. Broc Feeney put the #64 Ford Mustang into the 2’s with a 2.9, which would end up being that car’s fastest lap of the session, before Christopher Haase hit the front with a 2:02.28.

Marco Mapelli was the next driver into the 2’s with a 2:02.5768 in the #93 Wall Racing Lamborghini, setting down a marker for the rest of the field to chase with around 20 minutes left.

From then on, it was a battle to get into the top 17, with fast times coming in from everyone up and down the field. At the 20-minute remaining mark, a 2:04.6 was the time to beat to get into the top 17, but that was surely not going to remain for long.

The last 10 minutes were chaos on the timing screen as everyone up and down the field played their hand to try and get into the top 17.

Ryder Quinn in the #101 Q/Team MPC Audi was the big surprise, setting a string of quick laps ending with a 2:02.57 to go only five ten-thousandths slower than Mapelli, before Christopher Haase laid down another marker – a 2:02.51 – to go top.

Raffaele Marciello put the #46 WRT BMW into the 2:02’s with his only fast lap of the session, before Scott Andrews also landed the #44 Geyer Valmont/Tigani Mercedes into the 2:02 to go third.

Waters left his run to the penultimate lap of the session to eclipse the whole field, with attention quickly turning to 17th place to see who could make the cut-off. Kai Allen was outside the top 17 at the chequered flag in the #100 Grove Mercedes, but put in a 2:02.8 to end up in eighth place, knocking out the #47 Supabarn/Tigani Mercedes of David Russell.

Allen’s time put him just behind the #89 Team KRC BMW of Hesse, while Luca Stolz in the 75 Express Mercedes and Feeney’s early benchmark in the #64 HRT Ford Mustang were the other lap times in the 2:02s.

The #6 Tigani Motorsport Mercedes, the #32 WRT BMW, the #9 Hallmarc Audi, the #79 Tsunami RT Porsche, the #911 Absolute Racing Porsche and the #95 Optimum McLaren were the other cars to make the top 17, with Kirchhoefer’s cut-off time a 2:03.39.

Outside the top 17 were a number of big-name Pro-Class cars; Lucas Auer couldn’t get the #77 Craft Bamboo Mercedes into the top half, finishing with a 2:03.9 to go 26th, while the #2 Johor Motorsports Racing JMR Corvette at the hands of Earl Bamber only hit 23rd.

Jaxon Evans was the highest-placed Pro car to miss the cut; the #26 Arise Racing GT Ferrari driver was 20th after problems in Practice 5 earlier today limited their running. Also missing the cut was the #888 Team GMR Mercedes, with Martin’s early mark of a 2:03.9 the best that car could run.

Most cars had trouble-free sessions, the #27 Heart of Racing by SPS Mercedes only completed 5 laps and spent the last 40 minutes in the pits. At this stage, there’s no news as to why. The #61 EBM Porsche also suffered a delay, with a software update to the pit timer resulting in a complete failure of the dashboard of the car, requiring 13 minutes to reset.

Despite having to go through Qualifying 1, if these cars set a time good enough for the top 10, they will progress to the Pirelli Pole Shootout later today. Of course, they will have to do so while weaving through the Invitational and GT4 cars.

*RESULTS*

json.summary: Cam Waters set the fastest lap in final practice, securing the #222 Scott Taylor Mercedes the top spot. The session determined the top 17 cars advancing to the second qualifying round, with several major Pro-class entries failing to make the cut.

json.title: Mercedes-Benz profit drops 48.8% amid weak sales
json.content:
Mercedes-Benz profit drops 48.8% amid weak sales

The German carmaker posted revenue of €132.2bn ($156.78bn) and adjusted EBIT of €8.2bn for 2025, down 9.2% and 39.9% respectively year-on-year.

February 13, 2026 

Mercedes-Benz Cars recorded €4.8bn adjusted EBIT and a 5% adjusted return on sales. Credit: Mercedes-Benz 

Mercedes-Benz reported 2025 earnings within guidance as cost savings and new models offset weaker volumes and pricing pressure.

The German carmaker posted revenue of €132.2bn ($156.78bn) and adjusted EBIT of €8.2bn for 2025, down 9.2% and 39.9% respectively year-on-year.

It reflected the impact of global tariffs, foreign-exchange headwinds and intense competition in China.

Net profit declined 48.8% to €5.33bn.

Free cash flow from the industrial business totalled €5.4bn, compared with €9.2bn in 2024, while net liquidity rose to €32.2bn at year-end.

Mercedes-Benz proposed a dividend of €3.50 per share and said total shareholder return exceeded 20% in 2025.

Mercedes-Benz Cars recorded €4.8bn adjusted EBIT and a 5% adjusted return on sales (RoS), with unit sales falling 9.2% to 1.8 million vehicles.

Cost-efficiency actions under the Next Level Performance programme contributed more than €3.5bn to EBIT.

Mercedes-Benz Vans generated €1.75bn adjusted EBIT and a 10.2% adjusted RoS on sales of 359,136 units.

Mercedes-Benz Financial Services reported €1.27bn adjusted EBIT and a 9.7% adjusted return on equity (RoE).

During 2025, the group introduced new versions of the CLA, GLB and GLC, and presented an updated S-Class featuring MB.OS and fourth-generation MBUX.

It plans to launch more than 40 models by 2027, aiming for Mercedes-Benz Cars mid-term sales of about two million vehicles, a doubling of xEV share and over 15% growth in Top-End vehicles.

For 2026, Mercedes-Benz expects group revenue at the prior-year level and group EBIT “significantly above” 2025, while free cash flow from the industrial business is forecast slightly lower.

Guidance includes Mercedes-Benz Cars adjusted RoS of 3-5%, Vans 8-10% and financial services adjusted RoE of 10-12%.

Separately, Bloomberg reported that chief financial officer Harald Wilhelm said Mercedes-Benz intends to sell part of its roughly 35% holding in Daimler Truck this year to raise cash as sales and margins come under pressure.

The stake is valued at about €12bn, with proceeds to be returned to shareholders and further details expected in May.

The planned disposal comes as the carmaker prepares for a challenging year, having previously indicated margins are expected to be flat at best due to trade frictions and strong competitive pressure in China.

Just Auto has reached out to Mercedes-Benz for comment.
json.summary: Mercedes-Benz's 2025 net profit fell 48.8% to €5.33bn, with revenue and adjusted EBIT also declining. The automaker cited weak sales, global tariffs, and intense competition in China. It plans to sell part of its €12bn Daimler Truck stake this year to raise cash.

json.title: 2027 Mercedes-AMG GLC53 First Look: Hello, Inline-6 Engine
json.content:
Mercedes-Benz has already shown us the all-new 2027 GLC, riding on a new platform with promises of multiple powertrains and variants. And now we see one of those spin-offs: the 2027 Mercedes-AMG GLC53 that delves into the performance realm with a choice of SUV or coupe body styles when it goes on sale in the U.S. in the second half of 2026. It aims to take leadership in the segment.

The AMG is distinguished by its front fascia with a larger front splitter up front, as well as a larger lip on the rear spoiler on the roof (SUV) or trunklid (coupe) and a diffuser in glossy black.

The biggest change is the turbocharged four-cylinder engine that has been a Mercedes mainstay is gone. It is being discontinued because it will not meet future emissions regulations.

So, powering the 2027 GLC53 is Mercedes’ 3.0-liter turbocharged inline six-cylinder engine that has been given the AMG treatment. The result is a 443-hp, 443-lb-ft powerplant with a powerful exhaust note and an overboost function to deliver an extra adrenaline burst. The overboost provides 472 lb-ft of torque for 10 seconds to help make sprints in the passing lane even quicker.

Yup, The GLC Has a Drift Mode

The engine is paired with the AMG nine-speed automatic transmission and drives all four wheels via 4Matic all-wheel drive as standard. Customers can choose to add an electronically controlled limited slip differential that includes a Drift Mode and the ability to make the vehicle rear-wheel drive. These are firsts for an AMG SUV and come as part of the AMG Dynamics Plus package.

The I-6 has a turbocharger as well as an electric auxiliary compressor to help smooth the torque curve. The modified engine has a new cylinder head and intake camshaft. It is also deliberately louder, with an exhaust note that varies across the five available drive modes. The AMG Dynamic Plus package also adds a Race drive mode.

The second-generation integrated starter-generator takes on hybrid functions by supporting the engine at lower speeds with 23 hp and 151 lb-ft while also helping with energy recuperation and smoother start-stop transitions.

Standard rear-axle steering provides more agile turn-in, better handling, and a reduced turning circle.

Mercedes says the 2027 model ups the towing capability for the U.S. market (no figures yet) and is compatible with a Class II hitch.

A treat being offered: a special Golden Accents package, but only for the 2027 model year. It comes with a choice of an Obsidian Black Metallic or Graphite Grey Magno exterior with gold details for contrast, as well as AMG graphics.

The package also includes a lengthy list of equipment. It has 21-inch forged AMG cross-spoke wheels in matte black with gold rim flanges and center cap details. The brake calipers are black with white AMG branding. The fuel filler cap is silver chrome with black AMG design elements. Inside are AMG sport seats in black leather as well as contrast stitching throughout the cabin, right down to the floor mats. The carbon fiber trim is also woven with gold metallic threads. The door sill panels have an AMG logo illuminated in white.

The AMG Night Package is pretty much what you would expect: high-gloss black mirror housings and trim, dark chrome tailpipe trims and door handles, and an AMG emblem on the hood and badging on the rear in black chrome.

The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GLC53 will be available later in the second half of the year. Final pricing will be released closer to its on-sale date.

2027 Mercedes-AMG GLC 53 Specifications

BASE PRICE: $75,000 (est)

LAYOUT: Front-engine, AWD. 5-pass, 4-door SUV

ENGINE: 3.0L/443-hp/443-472 lb-ft turbo DOHC 24-valve I-6

TRANSMISSIONS: 9-speed auto

CURB WEIGHT: 5,000 lb (est)

WHEELBASE: 117.0 in (est)

L x W x H: 190.7 x 74.4 x 64.7 in (est)

0–60 MPH: 4.1 sec with race start (mfr)

EPA FUEL ECON: Not yet rated

EPA RANGE, COMB: N/A

ON SALE: Fall 2026
json.summary: The 2027 Mercedes-AMG GLC53 SUV/coupe replaces its turbo-four with a new 3.0-liter inline-six producing 443 hp and 472 lb-ft with overboost. It features a nine-speed automatic, standard AWD, an optional limited-slip diff with Drift Mode, and debuts a special Golden Accents package for the first model year. It goes on sale in the US in Fall 2026.

json.title: Kimi Antonelli makes '360 degree' Mercedes pledge after dropping to last in key F1 metric
json.content:
Kimi Antonelli has stated he will work “360 degrees” to get on top of the Mercedes challenger after enduring a difficult week in Bahrain.

The Italian ran into various issues throughout the three-day test, leaving him stationed in the garage for long periods.

Antonelli ended the week with just 82 laps to his name - the fewest lap count of all 22 drivers present at the pre-season test.

Despite his lack of on-track action, Antonelli ended the final day on Friday with the fastest lap of the test in his pocket.

As he comes to grips with the new cars this year built under a regulation change, Antonelli admitted he is enjoying the new feel.

“The car is lighter, it's a bit shorter, it's more agile,” Antonelli told media including RacingNews365.

“Low speed, the feeling is quite nice because you really feel the car being more agile. It's also the change of direction in Turns 6 and 7, the car is a lot quicker than last year.

“The speed is a bit less. But the car is quite nice to drive.”

Antonelli will return to the track next week for the final pre-season test ahead of the new season.

As he puts his final preparations in place, Antonelli acknowledged it will be a busy week of learning.

“On the power unit, it's a lot different,” he said. “Next week, I'm going to try to work on the long runs, because today on the C1 [tyre], I didn't do a great job on tyre management. 

“I will try to work 360 degrees as well, and try to work on single lap. Because today were my first three single laps, my first three qualifying [laps].

“We couldn't try before. But I'm going to try to work 360 degrees and trying to experiment all the possible scenarios.

“Melbourne is behind the door and it's going to be important.”
json.summary: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli logged the fewest laps of any driver in the Bahrain pre-season test but ended the week fastest. He pledged to work '360 degrees' on improving his single-lap pace and long-run tyre management ahead of the season.

json.title: Mercedes-AMG Boss Says Future Hi-Po Limited-Edition Black Series Cars Are an 'Obligation'
json.content:
The famed Black Series will be back, according to outgoing Mercedes-AMG CEO Michael Schiebe.  
He said the high-performance, limited-production cars will definitely carry on because Black Series is more than a brand, "it's an obligation."  
The 2021 Mercedes-AMG GT was the last car to get the Black Series treatment, and Schiebe said its successor "needs to be radical."  

It's been, like, six years since Mercedes-AMG last released a car from its revered Black Series. While some of us enthusiasts were rightfully worried that we might've seen the last of these desirable low-production, high-performance models, fear not, because outgoing AMG boss Michael Schiebe has confirmed that future Black Series cars are happening.  

Black Will Be Back

During a recent media event attended by Car and Driver, Schiebe—whose role as AMG CEO will go to Stefan Weckbach come July—was asked about where the Black Series stands amid the introduction of similarly themed brands such as Mythos. Without any hesitation, Schiebe said AMG definitely has plans for Black Series cars. "We have been very successful with it. This is such a strong brand, it's an obligation. If you want to develop a Black Series, then it really has to convince in terms of performance. It needs to be radical. But we want to definitely carry that into the future."  

Mercedes-AMG Vehicles For Sale Near You

See all results for used Mercedes-AMG for sale near 60323  

It's unclear when we'll see the first new Black Series, but it's possible that the Concept AMG GT Track Sport that was teased while testing last summer could be the answer hiding in plain sight. After all, it appears to meet one of the biggest requirements of being the most track-focused model, using the second-generation AMG GT as its foundation. Plus, the previous generation was the last car to get the special treatment, with the 2021 Mercedes-AMG GT Black Series boasting a big ol' rear wing, a 720-hp flat-plane-crank twin-turbo V-8, and setting a blistering time of 2:37.0 minutes at our 2022 Lightning Lap.  

Black Series Background

For anyone who wants a quick history lesson, the Black Series got its start with the Mercedes-Benz SLK55 AMG roadster. It featured a hand-built 400-hp 5.5-liter V-8 and received a rigorous weight-loss regimen. It wasn't sold in the United States, and only 120 copies were built between 2006 and 2007. That car was followed by the 2008 CLK63 AMG Black Series, which caused tarmac havoc with its 500-hp 6.2-liter V-8—built by hand, of course. Only 700 total examples exist.  

Mercedes-AMG

2009 Mercedes-Benz SL65 AMG Black Series

Next up was the gloriously wide SL65, with its twin-turbo 6.0-liter V-12 that produced 661 horsepower. Mercedes says the Black Series version only shared doors and side mirrors with the regular SL-class; 350 cars were sold worldwide. After that, the Black Series would enter hibernation until 2013, when it took on the C63. Along with a 510-hp 6.2-liter V-8, it was wider than the regular C-class and featured a coil-over suspension.  

Mercedes-AMG

2013 Mercedes-Benz AMG C63 Black Series

The 2014 SLS AMG Black Series (pictured at the top) is one of the most eye-catching models, largely thanks to its gullwing doors. Fewer than 200 versions made their way to America, and each featured a 622-hp 6.2-liter V-8.  

Black Series Reviews

Tracking the 2021 Mercedes-AMG GT Black Series  
Tested: 2014 Mercedes-Benz SLS AMG Black Series  
We Drive the Mercedes-Benz C63 AMG Black Series
json.summary: Outgoing Mercedes-AMG CEO Michael Schiebe has confirmed that the high-performance Black Series line will continue. He stated the series is an 'obligation' and future cars must be 'radical' in performance. The last model was the 2021 AMG GT Black Series.

json.title: Toto Wolff gives last-ditch effort as Mercedes F1 engine decision looms
json.content:
Toto Wolff gives last-ditch effort as Mercedes F1 engine decision looms

With a full investigation into the Mercedes engine and a potential regulation change looming, Toto Wolff is starting to sound concerned.

Mercedes has been the subject of many Formula 1 rumors over the past few weeks. Their engine for the 2026 season appears to be rather controversial, as they have reportedly found a loophole in the regulations to increase the compression ratio beyond 16:1.

While they managed to increase it to 18:1 under hotter conditions, it must remain at 16:1 when measured under normal temperatures. This discrepancy does not inherently violate the regulations, but several competitors have still deemed it to be unfair.

The FIA plan to step in and do a thorough inspection, given the widespread opposition. However, they do need four out of the five engine manufacturers to be in favor of a change for this to progress any further. Ferrari, Audi, and Honda are all in opposition, and Red Bull may be the deciding factor.

It is quite ironic, given the fact that Red Bull initially looked to be utilizing the same loophole as Mercedes, but they were apparently unsuccessful in implementing it as effectively. As a result, their decision to go against Mercedes could result in a regulation change, severely hurting the Silver Arrows and their customers.

Toto Wolff is deflecting as best as he can

The next round of testing in Bahrain has already gotten underway. Red Bull’s pace and power were quite strong, as Max Verstappen ended up near the top of the speed charts. The Dutchman was just over a tenth of a second behind McLaren's Lando Norris, who set the fastest time.

In light of tension inside the Mercedes garage, Toto Wolff was quick to call Red Bull the benchmark for comparison. Wolff was marveling over the RB22 and openly admired the power deployment on each lap.

The Mercedes team principal is playing it well with the media, as his comments suggest that Red Bull, not Mercedes, actually have the strongest engine.

It is a smart play, as the point is to show that Mercedes do not have an advantage as large as what others have been led to believe. The ultimate goal could be that by proving the advantage is rather minimal, so will the consequences.

A decision on the Mercedes engine is expected quite soon, and it could make or break the season of not only the factory team but of their three customer teams in McLaren, Alpine, and Williams as well. In the end, Red Bull could be the ultimate winner, and their stance could be monumental.
json.summary: Mercedes faces a potential 2026 engine regulation change after rivals challenged a technical loophole. Team principal Toto Wolff publicly downplays Mercedes' advantage by praising Red Bull's performance, in a strategic move ahead of a critical FIA decision requiring majority support from manufacturers.

json.title: F1 Testing: Mercedes set fastest times of week but George Russell warns of 'scary' Red Bull amid pecking order uncertainty
json.content:
F1 Testing: Mercedes set fastest times of week but George Russell warns of 'scary' Red Bull amid pecking order uncertainty

Kimi Antonelli and George Russell post quickest times of the first Bahrain test; Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton third ahead of McLaren, Red Bull; watch full live coverage from 7am-4pm on all three days of the final pre-season test in Bahrain from Wednesday on Sky Sports F1

Saturday 14 February 2026 07:25, UK

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Watch the morning highlights of the third day of the first Bahrain pre-season test.

Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli and George Russell set the fastest times on the final day of the first Bahrain test ahead of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton amid continued claims and counter claims from F1's four leading teams about who is really 2026's early leading force.

Russell had topped Friday's morning session with a then test-best quickest lap of 1:33.918 before team-mate Antonelli twice went faster during his afternoon in the car.

The Italian youngster finished up posting a 1:33.669 to set the benchmark for the first week of running in Sakhir.

Who set fastest times and who completed most laps at first Bahrain test?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Hamilton ran all day in the Ferrari SF-26 with his third-best time of 1:34.209 set during his morning's running.

The seven-time world champion racked up a mammoth 150 laps, although his day ended slightly prematurely when he had to park the car in a run-off area after it ran out of fuel with just over 10 minutes of the afternoon session to go.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player

Lewis Hamilton's final session was cut short after a car issue brought out the red flag.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri also had a busy full day of running and finished fourth fastest in the world champions' MCL40 after a day-high 161 laps, eight tenths slower than Antonelli.

Red Bull split their running between Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjkar and neither troubled the top of Friday's timesheet, both drivers finishing over 1.5s back on Antonelli's time in fifth and sixth places respectively.
